title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-03-21
taper: Recorded by Ken & Judy Lee on a Sony pc-124 cassette deck with Sony dynamic mics on Norelco cassettes. Microphones were set up in the balcony with a 10-20 foot spread.

ai_review.summary: Clear 1970 audience tape captures a fiery late‑show with smoking “Dancin’” jam, stellar Easy Wind and a remarkable Midnight Hour → Lovelight, while recording is good but shows occasional cut‑offs.
ai_review.review: The performance is hailed as one of the strongest early‑70 shows – first known rendition of Friend of the Devil, extended Dancin’ jam, superb Easy Wind, and a powerful Midnight Hour that morphs into Lovelight. The audience recording is generally clear for its era, though a few cuts and loud crowd noise are noted; overall it delivers an energetic listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars, praising the musical set‑list and energy; recording quality is consistently described as clear or good despite minor cut‑offs, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear for a 1970 audience tape; some reviewers note song cuts (Dancin’, Easy Wind) and occasional loud crowd noise, but overall the mix is listenable with decent instrument separation.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early acoustic‑folk material gives way to a jam‑heavy late set; extended Dancin’ and Easy Wind open the second half, followed by an energetic sequence of Cosmic Charlie, St. Stephen into Not Fade Away, and a powerful Midnight Hour that resolves into Lovelight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for perfect tone, melodic playing on Easy Wind and overall flawless performance.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for creative, peak‑era bass lines reminiscent of the Caution jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Delivered an outstanding solo during Easy Wind and helped drive crowd interaction.
